n4ad1c450b18.s: Which of the following pairs of parties founded by N.G. Ranga and their years is correctly matched?
n4ad1c450b18.x: Ranga founded the Krishikar Lok Party in 1951. He founded the Andhra Socialist Party in 1934 and the Swatantra Party in 1959, not 1949.

n40a30342943.s:
Arrange the following places in chronological order of the years associated with them in the socialist movement in Andhra:
1. Kankipadu (Rajakeeya Pathashala)
2. Kothapatnam
3. Madanapalle
n40a30342943.x: Kothapatnam is associated with 1937, Madanapalle with 1938 and the Kankipadu Rajakeeya Pathashala with 1939, so the order is 2, 3, 1.

nb842644d73e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
nb842644d73e.s: Which pair of leaders went with the CPI(M) after the 1964 split in the communist movement?
o: Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao
P. Sundarayya and Ravi Narayana Reddy
nb842644d73e.x: P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah went with the pro-China CPI(M), while Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao remained with the pro-Soviet CPI.

n7168cebf8ca.s: Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam of the Srikakulam struggle were killed on 10 July 1970 at:
n7168cebf8ca.x: Satyam and Kailasam were killed at Barikonda on 10 July 1970. Jalantra Kota is where Panchadhi Krishnamurthy was killed on 27 May 1969.

n1fc2b2c4055.s: Where was the Andhra Communist Party set up in January 1936?
n1fc2b2c4055.x: The Andhra Communist Party was set up at Kakinada in January 1936. Vijayawada hosted the second (1938) and third (1943) communist conferences.

n6ade0f7364d.s: Who presided over the 1935 Siricilla session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha?
n6ade0f7364d.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao presided at Siricilla in 1935. Ravi Narayana Reddy presided at Chilkur (1941) and Bhuvanagiri (1944), and K.V. Ranga Reddy at Hyderabad (1943).

n7c874310cb9.s: Who was the editor of Prajasakti, which began as a weekly in 1942 and became a daily in 1945?
n7c874310cb9.x: Prajasakti was edited by Maddukuri Chandrasekhara Rao. Chandra Rajeswara Rao edited Navasakti from Rajahmundry (1937).

n53070cd08e8.s: The Kalukova satyagraha at Munagala (1938) was led by:
n53070cd08e8.x: The Munagala (Kalukova) struggle was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao, backed by Chandra Rajeswara Rao. Peta Chapanayya was jailed in the Challapalli struggle of 1942.

n2ab906dcab3.s: At which 1944 session did the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha come under communist control, leading a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha to break away?
n2ab906dcab3.x: The 1944 Bhuvanagiri session brought the Mahasabha under communist control, after which a rival Nationalist Andhra Mahasabha broke away.

n79be0ead5c1.s: Communist activity in Andhra shifted the main focus of Andhra politics from ____ to ____.
n79be0ead5c1.x: Through peasant mobilisation, the communists shifted Andhra politics from language to land.

ne5f5117a99c.s: Who founded the People's War Group in 1980?
ne5f5117a99c.x: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the People's War Group in 1980. The other three were leaders of the Srikakulam Girijan struggle.

n4dee5cea450.s: Under the Communal Award, what percentage of seats in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province was earmarked for women?
n4dee5cea450.x: The Communal Award reserved three per cent of seats for women in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province.

nd47dfde6d59.s: Where did Gandhi begin his fast unto death against the Communal Award on 20 September 1932?
nd47dfde6d59.x: Gandhi began his fast unto death in Yerwada Jail, Poona, on 20 September 1932, arguing that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society.

n24ccdc32156.s: For purposes of representation, the Communal Award of 1932 divided Indians into how many groups?
n24ccdc32156.x: The Communal Award divided Indians into 11 groups and recognised the Depressed Classes as a minority.

nd1e8b07bbae.s: Under the Communal Award, the Depressed Classes were given:
o: A double vote – one in a separate electorate and one in the general electorate
A single vote in the general electorate only
Two votes, both restricted to the separate electorate
No vote, but nomination to provincial legislatures
nd1e8b07bbae.x: The Depressed Classes received a double vote: one in a separate electorate and another in the general electorate.

n7d73bb061d0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about provincial dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred subjects.
Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor with ministers.
Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with the Executive Council.
Local self-government was a reserved subject.
n7d73bb061d0.x: Local self-government was a transferred subject, administered by the Governor with ministers, not a reserved subject.

n6061c3c1c7d.s: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the demand of the ____ for a review of the 1919 Act.
n6061c3c1c7d.x: The Muddiman Committee (1924) was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the Government of India Act, 1919.

n410de35809f.s: The Simon Commission Report (1930) recommended replacing provincial dyarchy with:
o: Complete responsible government at the Centre
n410de35809f.x: The Simon Commission Report recommended abolishing provincial dyarchy in favour of provincial autonomy.

nacbc3f01bfb.s: Which of the following was a member of the seven-member Simon Commission?
nacbc3f01bfb.x: Clement Attlee was one of the seven British members of the Simon Commission, which was chaired by Sir John Simon.

n35c031cc974.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, how many members did the Viceroy's Executive Council have apart from the Commander-in-Chief?
n35c031cc974.x: Apart from the Commander-in-Chief, the Viceroy's Executive Council had six members, of whom three were Indians.

n5b0f474e268.s: The Simon Commission (1927) was appointed by the Conservative government of:
n5b0f474e268.x: The Conservative government of Stanley Baldwin appointed the Simon Commission on 8 November 1927, two years early, to review the 1919 Act.

n3b89db43218.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, dyarchy divided provincial subjects into:
n3b89db43218.x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces and divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.

n34b1ff96dac.s: Which of the following did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
o: Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League
n34b1ff96dac.x: The Justice Party (like Shafi's League faction) did not join the boycott, while Jinnah's faction and the Hindu Mahasabha joined it.

n3eea5c43480.s: The federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935 provided for dyarchy at:
o: Both the Centre and the provinces
n3eea5c43480.x: The 1935 Act provided dyarchy at the Centre, while replacing dyarchy in the provinces with provincial autonomy.

nc997afd2928.s: Provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 began in:
nc997afd2928.x: Provincial autonomy, which replaced dyarchy in the provinces, began in April 1937.

n328f64098bc.s: After the Congress ministries resigned, the Muslim League observed the 'Day of Deliverance' on:
n328f64098bc.x: The League observed 22 December 1939 as the Day of Deliverance after the Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939.

n7bf4df4be8c.s: The dyarchy scheme of the Government of India Act, 1919 is named after Edwin Montagu and:
n7bf4df4be8c.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms are named after Secretary of State Edwin Montagu and Viceroy Lord Chelmsford.

n48cc706b5c9.s: The Public Service Commission provided for under Section 96(C) of the 1919 Act was set up on 1 October:
n48cc706b5c9.x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission, not in 1921 when the Act came into force.

ndb7e1fd202b.s: The Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal) was set up by royal proclamation in:
ndb7e1fd202b.x: The Chamber of Princes, a consultative body of Indian rulers, was set up in 1921 under the 1919 reforms, not under the 1935 Act.

n1fb73081751.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the reaction to the Nehru Report is correctly matched?
o: Rejection of the Nehru Report – Muslim League
One-year ultimatum to Britain – Muslim League
n1fb73081751.x: The Muslim League rejected the Nehru Report. Nehru and Bose demanded complete independence, Congress gave Britain a one-year ultimatum, and complete independence was declared at Lahore in 1929.

n04630fd37e0.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
n04630fd37e0.s: The Simon Commission report recommended the creation of which new province?
n04630fd37e0.x: The report recommended creating Orissa as a province (and separating Sindh and Burma), but ignored Andhra's demand for a separate province.

nd777eff1996.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded what share of Muslim representation at the Centre?
nd777eff1996.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded one-third Muslim representation at the Centre, along with provincial residuary powers, separate electorates and safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces.

n4ce5f9f8f31.s: On the question of electorates, the Delhi Proposals supported:
n4ce5f9f8f31.x: The Delhi Proposals supported joint electorates subject to safeguards such as the separation of Sindh and one-third Muslim representation at the Centre.

n22e3e0a902a.s: The Second Round Table Conference ended in a deadlock over:
n22e3e0a902a.x: The Second Round Table Conference ended in a deadlock over the minorities question; the federal structure had been agreed at the First Conference.

ncea40c63d1f.s: The Deepavali Declaration of 1929 was issued by:
ncea40c63d1f.x: Lord Irwin issued the Deepavali Declaration in 1929, promising a Round Table Conference after the Simon Commission report.

nf2c4cc52c10.s: Who served as secretary of the committee that drafted the Nehru Report?
nf2c4cc52c10.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary; the report recommended a Supreme Court and proposed ending dyarchy.

n12b3248d4ed.s: The Nehru Report, drafted by a committee chaired by Motilal Nehru, was published in:
n12b3248d4ed.x: The Nehru Report came out in August 1928; 1929 is a known trap.

n42671327c04.s: Which group lobbied the Simon Commission and saw its provincial demand supported in the report?
n42671327c04.x: The Oriyas lobbied the Simon Commission and the report supported the creation of Orissa; the Andhras boycotted it and their demand was ignored.

na1b61e78afa.s: The three Round Table Conferences in London were held under which British Prime Minister?
na1b61e78afa.x: All three Round Table Conferences were held in London under Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.

n3dc59edc1f3.s: On electorates, the Simon Commission report recommended:
n3dc59edc1f3.x: The report recommended continuing separate communal electorates, along with abolition of dyarchy and provincial autonomy.

n507927d292b.shape: one-liner (NOT not possible: the original has no false statement to use)
n507927d292b.s: Who first raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934?
n507927d292b.x: M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand in 1934; the Congress adopted it officially in 1935.

ncdeb402f31e.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Muslim League observes Deliverance Day
2. Resignation of the Congress ministries
3. Linlithgow declares India a party to the Second World War
4. Adoption of the Lahore Resolution
ncdeb402f31e.x: Linlithgow declared India a party to the war in September 1939, the ministries resigned in October-November 1939, Deliverance Day was 22 December 1939 and the Lahore Resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940.

n50b6c2c77e3.s: The Sri Bagh Pact (November 1937) was concluded at the house of:
n50b6c2c77e3.x: The pact, which sought to close the Coastal-Rayalaseema rift, was concluded at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house 'Sreerbagh', not Prakasam's.

n55abe8fdba7.s: 'Begar', abolished by the Congress ministries of 1937-39, was:
n55abe8fdba7.x: Begar was forced labour, not a salt tax; the Congress ministries abolished it.

na255c144721.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the:
na255c144721.x: Residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General, not in the provinces.

n869f606043a.s: In how many of the eleven provinces did the Congress form ministries after the 1937 elections?
n869f606043a.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces, including Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, UP, NWFP and Assam.

n908011aedb2.s: How many subjects did the Federal List contain under the Government of India Act, 1935?
n908011aedb2.x: The Federal List had 59 subjects, the Provincial List 54 and the Concurrent List 36.

n78d0832dbfe.s: Which party formed the ministry in the Madras Presidency after the 1937 elections?
n78d0832dbfe.x: The Congress formed the Madras ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out and the People's Party lost all its seats.

n3bc325674c5.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 gave Muslims what share of seats in the Federal Legislature?
n3bc325674c5.x: The 1935 Act gave Muslims 33% of the seats in the Federal Legislature, extending separate electorates further.

nc050be10001.s: Who moved the Lahore Resolution on 23 March 1940?
nc050be10001.x: A.K. Fazlul Huq moved the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution; Sikandar Hayat Khan drafted it and Jinnah presided.

nb8b927342f0.s: Who wrote 'Pakistan or the Partition of India'?
nb8b927342f0.x: B.R. Ambedkar wrote Pakistan or the Partition of India; Rahmat Ali wrote Now or Never and Rafiq Zakaria wrote The Man Who Divided India.

nindian-history-100-2.s: Gandhi's first settlement, set up near Durban in 1904, was:
nindian-history-100-2.x: Phoenix near Durban (1904) was Gandhi's first settlement; Tolstoy Farm near Johannesburg was set up in 1910 with Kallenbach.

nbe522fd80cd.s: Which Act of 1914 abolished the £3 poll tax and recognised Indian marriages in South Africa?
nbe522fd80cd.x: The Indian Relief Act of 1914, which followed the Great March of 1913, both abolished the poll tax and recognised Indian marriages.

nindian-history-100-14.x: Gandhi called Yerawada Jail 'Mandir'. Sabarmati was also called Satyagraha Ashram and Sadaqat Ashram was linked with his Bihar work.

nb6dec4179cf.s: Which work inspired Gandhi's ideas of the dignity of labour and Sarvodaya?
o: Tolstoy's The Kingdom of God Is Within You
nb6dec4179cf.x: John Ruskin's Unto This Last inspired Gandhi's ideas of the dignity of labour and Sarvodaya; Thoreau's Civil Disobedience gave him the right to break unjust laws.

n9f50904f3bf.s: In which year did Gandhi go to South Africa for Dada Abdullah's case?
n9f50904f3bf.x: After his practice in Rajkot and Bombay did not succeed, Gandhi went to South Africa in 1893 for Dada Abdullah's case.

nindian-history-7-14.s: The newspaper Swadeshabhimani was edited by:
nindian-history-7-14.x: Swadeshabhimani was edited by Ramakrishna Pillai. Vande Matram was Aurobindo's English paper; Harijan Bandhu and Harijan Sewak were Gandhi's Gujarati and Hindi papers.

n323e99fa070.s: Who called Gandhi a 'half-naked fakir' in 1931?
n323e99fa070.x: Winston Churchill, not Lord Irwin, called Gandhi a 'half-naked fakir' in 1931.

na06a21892ed.s: In which year did Gandhi undergo his first jail term in South Africa?
na06a21892ed.x: Gandhi's first jail term was in 1908, after the burning of registration certificates; 1913 was the year of the Great March.

n612b7cefb5c.s: In which language did Gandhi originally write Hind Swaraj in 1909?
n612b7cefb5c.x: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in Gujarati in 1909 aboard the Kildonan Castle and translated it into English himself; Bombay banned it in 1910.

nd03115397f0.s: Gandhi's Hind Swaraj presents swaraj as:
nd03115397f0.x: Hind Swaraj presents swaraj as self-rule and advocates self-reliance and rural life, while critiquing industrialisation.

n5b67ed8c07b.s: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 at:
n5b67ed8c07b.x: Gandhi was born at Porbandar; Rajkot was where he later practised and Bhavnagar is where he studied at Samaldas College.

nindian-history-109-13.s: The Urdu journal Al-Hilal was associated with:
nindian-history-109-13.x: Al-Hilal was Abul Kalam Azad's Urdu journal; Young India, Navajivan and Indian Opinion were Gandhi's.

n6aaa220f6bd.s: Gandhi returned his Kaisar-i-Hind gold medal in:
n6aaa220f6bd.x: Gandhi returned the medal (awarded in 1915 for his South African ambulance work) in 1920 during the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation campaign.

n7fe1fdfe1f8.s: Which country is regarded as the 'laboratory' where Gandhi developed satyagraha in 1906?
n7fe1fdfe1f8.x: Gandhi developed and experimented with satyagraha in South Africa in 1906, which is why South Africa is called its laboratory.

ndd965c680e2.s: The journals Indian Opinion, Navajivan and Harijan are associated with:
ndd965c680e2.x: Indian Opinion, Navajivan and Harijan are associated with Gandhi's journalistic work.

n4d53bde9af3.shape: one-liner (match not possible: the facts do not form four pairs)
n4d53bde9af3.s: When the only alternatives were cowardice and violence, Gandhi said he would prefer:
n4d53bde9af3.x: Gandhi preferred violence to cowardice when those were the only alternatives; for him ahimsa was a quality of the strong, not of the weak.

n1260056cd85.s: 'Trusteeship' as the basis of property relations is a concept of:
n1260056cd85.x: Trusteeship is Gandhian; Marxism seeks the abolition of private property.

n57f825bf38c.s: Gandhi's Talisman asks a person, before taking a step, to recall the face of:
n57f825bf38c.x: Gandhi's Talisman requires one to consider the poorest and weakest person before taking a step.

n32b797de5ec.s: Gandhi held that politics bereft of religion is a ____.
n32b797de5ec.x: Gandhi said politics bereft of religion (meaning morality based on truth and non-violence) is a death-trap.

n47fea7e2d25.s: The early English rendering of 'Satyagraha' was:
n47fea7e2d25.x: Satyagraha, born in 1906 in the Transvaal, was early rendered in English as 'passive resistance'.

n195d5847b6f.s: Gandhi is called a philosophical anarchist because of his ideal of:
n195d5847b6f.x: His ideal of 'enlightened anarchy' and his view of the State as violence in concentrated form make Gandhi a philosophical anarchist.

ncbc3016a5d9.s: According to Gandhi, the nature of the end is determined by the nature of the:
ncbc3016a5d9.x: Gandhi held that means are everything and that the end reflects the means used to attain it.

n598c440374f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gandhian trusteeship?
o: It sought class harmony rather than class struggle.
Its roots lay in the Gita's idea of non-possession and the English law of trusts.
It was applied only to zamindars and not to capitalists.
It was applied to mill owners such as those of Ahmedabad.
n598c440374f.x: Trusteeship was applied to both capitalists and zamindars (e.g. the Ahmedabad mill owners), not only to zamindars.

nf09abcbab6b.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Gandhi's ideas is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Term 'bread labour' – T.M. Bondaref, via Tolstoy
Bread labour – the Gita's idea of yajna
Right to break unjust laws – Thoreau's Civil Disobedience
nf09abcbab6b.x: The sources of bread labour were Tolstoy (from Bondaref) and Ruskin's Unto This Last, linked by Gandhi to yajna; Thoreau's work gave the right to break unjust laws.

n2711e1fea24.s: Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan movement began in 1951 at:
n2711e1fea24.x: Bhoodan began at Pochampalli (now in Telangana) in 1951.

nf34498b1ac7.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education is correctly matched?
o: Duration of free and compulsory education – five years
nf34498b1ac7.x: The Wardha Scheme was drawn up by the Zakir Hussain Committee, adopted in 1937 and envisaged seven years of free and compulsory education.

n130456bfa55.s: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932)?
n130456bfa55.x: G.D. Birla was its first president and Amritlal Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa) its secretary; Gandhi founded it after the Poona Pact.

n87fd74719a9.s: What was Gandhi's stand on the remarriage of child widows?
o: He left it to caste panchayats
n87fd74719a9.x: Gandhi opposed purdah, child marriage and dowry but supported the remarriage of child widows.

o: A matter for the State alone
n8631d951a06.x: Gandhi called untouchability 'a blot on Hinduism' and sought reform from within Hindu society.

nab0e8a128b9.s: Gandhi's fasts during the communal riots of 1946-47 were held at Calcutta and:
nab0e8a128b9.x: His riot-time fasts of 1946-47 were at Calcutta and Noakhali, not Vaikom or Guruvayur.

nc8cca7b5b55.s: In Andhra, the Desasevikalu functioned as a:
nc8cca7b5b55.x: Desasevikalu was a women's wing; Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921 and Andhra women donated jewellery to the Tilak Fund.

nf3652532350.s: Which term used by Gandhi was rejected by Ambedkar and Dalit leaders, who criticised caste-Hindu paternalism?
nf3652532350.x: Ambedkar and Dalit leaders rejected the term 'Harijan' and criticised what they saw as caste-Hindu paternalism.

nindian-history-132-17.s: Where was the 'Do or Die' call of the Quit India Movement given in 1942?
nindian-history-132-17.x: The Quit India Movement began with the 'Do or Die' call at Bombay in 1942.

n77b240d1184.s: The Champaran Satyagraha was directed mainly against:
o: Forced indigo cultivation and illegal exactions by European planters
n77b240d1184.x: European planters compelled peasants to grow indigo and, when indigo became unprofitable, demanded illegal dues and enhanced rents; forest tax was not the issue.

nindian-history-122-8.s: Which Amritsar leader was arrested in April 1919, before the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
nindian-history-122-8.x: Dr Saifuddin Kitchlew was the Amritsar leader arrested on 9 April 1919, before the massacre.

nindian-history-132-11.s: In which year did the Champaran Satyagraha take place in Bihar?
nindian-history-132-11.x: Champaran was in 1917; Kheda and the Ahmedabad Mill Strike followed in 1918.

nf170e2e9202.s: Gandhi's return to India on 9 January 1915 is now observed as:
nf170e2e9202.x: 9 January, the day Gandhi returned in 1915, is observed as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

n26f726c1b53.s: What wage rise did the tribunal award the workers in the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918)?
n26f726c1b53.x: The workers had demanded 50%; Gandhi advised 35% and the tribunal awarded 35%.

nafcbd19283b.s: Who provided field leadership to the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918?
nafcbd19283b.x: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel gave field leadership as Kheda peasants refused to pay land revenue despite threats of confiscation.

n2269387be3b.s: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
n2269387be3b.x: Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy when the massacre took place at Amritsar.

o: Lump-sum compensation demanded when indigo lost its value
ne6721a7fba5.x: Tawan was lump-sum compensation extracted when indigo became less valuable; sharahbeshi was enhanced rent.

n4792af99387.s: Who chaired the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (1917), on which Gandhi represented the ryots?
n4792af99387.x: F.G. Sly chaired the committee, appointed by the Bihar and Orissa government.

n5a67e88b9e6.s: After the Hunter Committee condemned General Dyer's conduct, which body backed him?
n5a67e88b9e6.x: The Hunter Committee, appointed after the massacre, condemned Dyer, but the House of Lords supported him.

nindian-history-95-10.s: Which movement demanded the immediate end of British rule?
nindian-history-95-10.x: The Quit India Movement demanded the immediate end of British rule; Non-Cooperation was non-violent non-cooperation.

nindian-history-95-12.s: The Home Rule Movement of 1916 aimed at:
nindian-history-95-12.x: The Home Rule Movement sought self-government; the immediate end of British rule was the demand of Quit India.

nindian-history-122-10.s: Who was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
nindian-history-122-10.x: Michael O'Dwyer was Lieutenant Governor of Punjab; Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the firing.

nindian-history-122-3.s: The crowd at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April 1919 had gathered on the occasion of:
nindian-history-122-3.x: The crowd gathered on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919, amid the Rowlatt Satyagraha protests and arrests of local leaders.

nb80747a5dda.s: Gandhi's Satyagraha Ashram, established in 1915, was at:
nb80747a5dda.x: The Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab was set up in 1915, followed by Sabarmati (1917) and Sevagram (1936).

nindian-history-100-26.s: Gandhi first used a hunger strike as a weapon during the:
nindian-history-100-26.x: Gandhi's fast at Ahmedabad in 1918, during the mill workers' dispute, was his first hunger strike used as a weapon.

n7f892b24bd9.s: Which of the following took place first?
n7f892b24bd9.x: Champaran (1917) came first, followed by the Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb-Mar 1918), Kheda (1918) and the Rowlatt Satyagraha (April 1919).

nindian-history-100-28.s: The main condition behind the Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was:
nindian-history-100-28.x: Crop failure in Kheda in 1918 made revenue payment hard, so peasants demanded remission or suspension of land revenue.

nindian-history-100-4.s: Under the Tinkathia system in Champaran, peasants were forced to grow indigo on what portion of their land?
nindian-history-100-4.x: The Tinkathia system forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land.

n433e4509567.s: The Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolished:
n433e4509567.x: Based on the Enquiry Committee's recommendations, the Act abolished Tinkathia and secured a 25 per cent refund of illegal exactions.

n88ff21b936e.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale was Gandhi's political mentor; Tolstoy, Ruskin and Thoreau were his intellectual influences.

nbe5af635e61.s: Who among the following was a member of the Congress's Punjab Sub-Committee that inquired into the Punjab events?
nbe5af635e61.x: The Punjab Sub-Committee comprised Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Abbas Tyabji, M.R. Jayakar and Gandhi; the other three were Indian members of the official Hunter Committee.

nindian-history-122-12.s: The report of the Congress's non-official inquiry into the Jallianwala Bagh incident was drafted by:
nindian-history-122-12.x: Gandhi drafted the report of the Congress Inquiry Committee; the Hunter Committee, chaired by Lord William Hunter, was the official inquiry.

ncc694e8794e.s: Under the Rowlatt Act, in-camera trials were held by a High Court panel of how many judges?
ncc694e8794e.x: The Rowlatt Act provided in-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel, with no right of appeal.

na87e78982fb.s: The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919) was repealed during the viceroyalty of:
na87e78982fb.x: It was repealed under Lord Reading, along with the Press Act of 1910.

n7a78dedc524.s: Which of the following was an Indian member of the Hunter Committee?
n7a78dedc524.x: Chimanlal Setalvad, Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmed Khan were the Indian members; their minority report was more critical of Dyer.

nindian-history-122-18.s: Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer on 13 March 1940 at:
nindian-history-122-18.x: Udham Singh killed Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall, London, on 13 March 1940.

nbf7b671167a.s: Martial law in Amritsar and Lahore after 13 April 1919 included public floggings, aircraft strafing and the humiliating ____ order.
nbf7b671167a.x: Martial law included public floggings, aircraft strafing of protestors and the crawling order.

nindian-history-122-17.s: Who resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
nindian-history-122-17.x: Sir Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest; Montagu called the firing 'preventive murder'.

nindian-history-26-2-18.s: The Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922 led Gandhi to withdraw the:
nindian-history-26-2-18.x: The Chauri Chaura violence of February 1922 made Gandhi withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement.

nindian-history-122-20.s: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre formed an important background to which movement?
nindian-history-122-20.x: By deepening hostility to British rule, the massacre prepared the ground for the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920.

nf9442721c70.s: In which year did the Dandi March take place?
nf9442721c70.x: The Dandi March was in 1930, after the Swadeshi Movement (1905) and Jallianwala Bagh (1919) and before Quit India (1942).

nindian-history-122-23.s: The Hunter Committee described General Dyer's action as:
nindian-history-122-23.x: The Hunter Committee criticised Dyer by calling his action an 'error of judgement'; 'preventive murder' was Montagu's phrase.

nindian-history-122-5.s: Which Act was popularly described as 'No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel'?
nindian-history-122-5.x: The Rowlatt Act was called 'No Vakil, No Appeal, No Daleel' because it allowed detention without trial; Gandhi responded with the Rowlatt Satyagraha.

n1375d63009c.s: What was the outcome of the Hunter Committee inquiry for General Dyer?
o: He was fully exonerated and retained in command
He was censured and relieved of command but received no real punishment
He was sentenced to life imprisonment
He was promoted to Lieutenant Governor of Punjab
n1375d63009c.x: Dyer was censured and relieved of command but not really punished; the House of Lords backed him and Gandhi called the findings a whitewash.

nb67d422d57b.s:
Assertion (A): The Nagpur session of the Congress (December 1920) organised Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines.
Reason (R): The Nagpur session fixed the Congress membership fee at one rupee.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nb67d422d57b.x: The Nagpur session reorganised Congress units on linguistic lines, but the membership fee was fixed at four annas, not one rupee.

n2380d3288ac.s: Under the Non-Cooperation programme, the November 1920 legislative elections were:
n2380d3288ac.x: The November 1920 elections were boycotted; surrender of titles and non-payment of taxes (as the final stage) were part of the programme.

nfb9b91b41a9.s: The Bardoli resolution was adopted on:
nfb9b91b41a9.x: The Bardoli resolution was adopted on 11–12 February 1922; the Prince of Wales boycott was on 17 November 1921 and the Treaty of Sevres in May 1920.

n78556e1c470.s: During the Non-Cooperation Movement, tribals and forest users participated through opposition to:
n78556e1c470.x: Tribals and forest users joined the movement by opposing pullari, while peasants joined no-tax campaigns.

n0b08df628b0.s: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in which district of the United Provinces?
n0b08df628b0.x: Chauri Chaura is in Gorakhpur district, where a crowd burnt the police station after police action against a procession in February 1922.

nb9d3a1c0631.s: Which leader of the Non-Cooperation era was associated with Madras and later became a No-Changer?
nb9d3a1c0631.x: Rajagopalachari (Madras) became a No-Changer; C.R. Das (Bengal) and Motilal Nehru (UP) became Swarajists.

nb54f82a40ae.s: In the Great Trial at Ahmedabad (March 1922), Gandhi was sentenced to:
nb54f82a40ae.x: Charged with sedition under Section 124A for his Young India articles, Gandhi received a six-year sentence.

ne966df63f27.s: The Akali Movement for gurdwara reform led to the Sikh Gurdwaras Act of:
ne966df63f27.x: The Akali Movement (1920–25) against corrupt mahants culminated in the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.

n5376427d04e.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the day of the death of:
n5376427d04e.x: The movement was launched on 1 August 1920, the day Tilak died; the Calcutta special session approved it in September 1920.

n98690c3dd11.s: Gujarat Vidyapith, a national institution of the Non-Cooperation era, was founded in:
n98690c3dd11.x: Gujarat Vidyapith was founded in 1920, while Kashi and Bihar Vidyapiths came in 1921.

n063f85d8c7a.s: Who called the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement after Chauri Chaura a 'national calamity'?
n063f85d8c7a.x: Subhas Chandra Bose called the withdrawal a national calamity; M.N. Roy described it as weak leadership.

n5bc25397e43.s: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the MAO College, from which Aligarh Muslim University developed, in:
n5bc25397e43.x: The MAO College was established in 1875; the university got legal status in 1920 but was not a Non-Cooperation national institution.

n2218e19a6ef.s: Gandhi's Great Trial of 1922 was presided over by Judge:
n2218e19a6ef.x: Judge C.N. Broomfield presided over the Great Trial on 18 March 1922, where Gandhi pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty.

n7daebbb62d9.s: Who led the Palnadu forest satyagraha?
n7daebbb62d9.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha, which involved boycotting forest officials and refusing the grazing tax.

nap-history-25-5.s: Who led the Kisan (agrarian) movement in Andhra?
nap-history-25-5.x: N.G. Ranga led the Kisan movement; Veerayya Chowdary led the No-Tax Campaign and Kanneganti Hanumanthu the Palnadu forest satyagraha.

nap-history-25-4.s: The Salt Satyagraha centre Mypadu was located in the region of:
nap-history-25-4.x: Mypadu was in Nellore; Chinnapuram was near Machilipatnam and Devarampadu near Ongole.

nap-history-25-23.x: Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary, who led the No-Tax Campaign at Pedanandipadu in Guntur, was called Andhra Shivaji.

na006b887bb4.s: Which of the following was part of the constructive programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: Promotion of khadi and the charkha
na006b887bb4.x: Promotion of khadi and the charkha was constructive work; boycott of foreign cloth was a boycott measure.

n3ac432ba3ad.s: Which of the following gave up legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
n3ac432ba3ad.x: T. Prakasam was among the lawyers who gave up practice, along with Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Rajagopalachari, Patel and others; Ambedkar was not.

n9c53a1e1536.s: Which of the following was a background factor behind the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
n9c53a1e1536.x: The Khilafat issue, along with the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was a cause of the movement; the Simon Commission Report was not.

nd568e8e128d.s: The AICC meeting at Vijayawada (1921) set a target of how many charkhas?
nd568e8e128d.x: The Vijayawada targets were one crore rupees for the Tilak Swaraj Fund, one crore members and twenty lakh charkhas.

n707c34e8e19.s: Who founded the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party along with C.R. Das?
n707c34e8e19.x: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru were the principal founders of the Swaraj Party; Jawaharlal Nehru was not a founder.

n34129a7a520.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
n34129a7a520.s: Who reacted to the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement with 'amazement and consternation'?
n34129a7a520.x: Jawaharlal Nehru reacted with 'amazement and consternation'; Bose called it a national tragedy and M.N. Roy blamed weak leadership.

n0120d6849c1.s: Which of the following places was covered in Gandhi's October 1921 tour of Andhra?
n0120d6849c1.x: In October 1921 Gandhi toured Kurnool, Kadapa, Tirupati and Tadipatri; Kakinada, Eluru and Machilipatnam were on his April coastal tour.

n2024bf8c846.s: The flag design of Pingali Venkayya endorsed by Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting (1921) carried the:
n2024bf8c846.x: Pingali Venkayya's design endorsed by Gandhi at Vijayawada had the charkha.

nbd0d2223cad.s: Kanneganti Hanumanthu, hero of the Palnadu Pullari satyagraha (1921-22), was born in which district?
nbd0d2223cad.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu was born in Guntur district, where Palnadu, the site of Andhra's first forest satyagraha, lies.

n8f351ca7fd6.s: During the Palnadu Pullari satyagraha, the 300 cattle driven into the forest without paying the tax were impounded at:
n8f351ca7fd6.x: The cattle were impounded at Minchalapadu; Macherla was where officials were socially boycotted.

n9f3e155bf6b.s: Who was the President of the Swarajist party organisation in Andhra?
n9f3e155bf6b.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was President, Unnava Lakshminarayana Secretary and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao Treasurer.

n57c81bfea53.s: Which bill of 1928 did the Swarajists oppose in the Central Legislative Assembly?
n57c81bfea53.x: The Swarajists opposed the Public Safety Bill of 1928; earlier, their demand for review of the 1919 Act led to the Muddiman Committee.

n7166bb839d6.s: Which of the following was a part of the constructive programme of the 1920s national movement?
n7166bb839d6.x: The constructive programme included khadi and spinning, removal of untouchability, Hindu-Muslim unity, prohibition, national schools and village panchayats.

n1f25eaede97.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Lord Irwin – release of non-violent political prisoners
Gandhi – suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement
Lord Irwin – commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades
Gandhi – attending the Second Round Table Conference
n1f25eaede97.x: Irwin refused to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades; he did agree to release non-violent prisoners, remit fines, return unsold lands and permit limited salt-making.

n72497c7f876.s: The Lahore Session of the Congress (December 1929) adopted:
n72497c7f876.x: With the one-year Calcutta ultimatum expired, the Lahore Session rejected Dominion Status and adopted Purna Swaraj.

n337a54e6288.s: Which Salt Satyagraha camp was called the 'Andhra Dandi'?
n337a54e6288.x: Seethanagaram Ashram (Brahmajosyula Subrahmanyam), the East Godavari camp, was the 'Andhra Dandi'; Devarampadu was the 'Dakshina Dandi'.

ne3a589a0d35.s: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Gandhi agreed to attend which Round Table Conference?
ne3a589a0d35.x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference.

n3faedbdc636.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Congress in December 1929?
n3faedbdc636.x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided at Lahore and hoisted the tricolour on the banks of the Ravi; Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee.

n583af1cc06a.s: The National Economic Programme resolution passed at the Karachi Session (March 1931) was drafted by:
n583af1cc06a.x: Jawaharlal Nehru drafted the National Economic Programme, passed at Karachi with the resolution on Fundamental Rights.

n926e6318657.s: In which year did the Cripps Mission come to India?
n926e6318657.x: The Cripps Mission came in 1942, after Chauri Chaura (1922), the Lahore Session (1929) and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

n4a66d8f4e20.s: The Poona Pact was signed in:
n4a66d8f4e20.x: The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932; the Communal Award was announced in August 1932.

n2650a83ba1e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
n2650a83ba1e.s: Which of the following describes women's role in the Andhra Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: They took part only in symbolic gatherings
They joined in large numbers, making salt, picketing and courting imprisonment
Their role was confined to national leaders outside Andhra
n2650a83ba1e.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement brought women into the Andhra struggle in large numbers, including salt-making, picketing and imprisonment.

n521a082da33.s: How many followers accompanied Gandhi on the Dandi March (12 March–6 April 1930)?
n521a082da33.x: Gandhi marched with 78 followers, covering about 240 miles.

ndcb1f8b9be9.s: Which of the following was part of the Civil Disobedience programme in Andhra villages?
ndcb1f8b9be9.x: The programme included making salt, picketing foreign-cloth and toddy shops, cutting toddy palms and raiding salt depots.

n44e17db3228.s: Who was the sole representative of the Congress at the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
n44e17db3228.x: Gandhi was the sole Congress representative; Sarojini Naidu represented Indian women and Malaviya also attended.

n03a658be114.s: After mass Civil Disobedience was suspended on 14 July 1933, the movement was formally withdrawn in:
n03a658be114.x: The movement was formally withdrawn in April 1934, and the Congress then contested the 1934 Central Assembly elections.

nindian-history-111-18.s: 'Purna Swaraj', adopted as the Congress goal, meant:
nindian-history-111-18.x: Purna Swaraj meant Complete Independence as the Congress goal.

na4f1d2ea4fd.s: Which of the following was included in the Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme?
o: Separate electorates for the depressed classes
na4f1d2ea4fd.x: The Karachi resolution included civil liberties, universal adult franchise, religious neutrality and free primary education.

nbc7b04aafd7.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
nbc7b04aafd7.s: Under the Cripps proposals, defence and control of the army during the interim period were to remain with:
nbc7b04aafd7.x: Defence and the army were to stay with Britain in the interim, and the Governor-General's powers were retained.

nee5d6ca8cf3.s: Who were the Congress negotiators with the Cripps Mission?
nee5d6ca8cf3.x: Nehru and Azad negotiated for the Congress, which objected to the right to secede and to the absence of an immediate transfer of power.

na3886a92e01.s: Which Viceroy declared India a party to the Second World War without consulting Indian leaders?
na3886a92e01.x: Lord Linlithgow's declaration led to the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939.

ne4b842b248b.s: The Cripps proposals promised India ____ after the war.
ne4b842b248b.x: The proposals promised dominion status after the war and allowed the Indian Union the power to secede.

nindian-history-130-18.s: What was the outcome of the Cripps proposals of 1942?
o: They were rejected and the negotiations failed
They were accepted by the Congress
They led to an immediate interim government
They were accepted by the Muslim League alone
nindian-history-130-18.x: The Cripps proposals, which offered post-war Dominion Status and let provinces opt out of the Union, were rejected and the talks failed.

n98c1c8ec440.s: The Ramgarh session of the Congress, held between the resignation of the ministries and the August Offer, took place in:
n98c1c8ec440.x: The ministries resigned in October–November 1939, the Ramgarh session was in March 1940, the August Offer in August 1940 and the Cripps Mission in March–April 1942.

ncf36ff06b7e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
ncf36ff06b7e.s: Which of the following stayed away from the Quit India Movement?
ncf36ff06b7e.x: The Muslim League, the Hindu Mahasabha and the princely states stayed away from the movement.

n37e14db2a85.s: During the Quit India Movement, where was the Madras–Puri passenger train burnt after police firing on 12 August 1942?
n37e14db2a85.x: Tenali saw firing on 12 August 1942 and the burning of the Madras–Puri train; Guntur had firing on 13 August and Bhimavaram on 17 August.

n18af581dcad.s: During the Quit India Movement, Gandhi instructed government servants to:
o: Stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress
n18af581dcad.x: Government servants were told to stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress; soldiers were not to fire on Indians.

nebd412e1f0e.s: Gandhi's fast at the Aga Khan Palace from February 1943 lasted:
nebd412e1f0e.x: Gandhi undertook a 21-day fast against state violence, and three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council resigned in this context.

nindian-history-113-16.s: Who said, 'Library Movement in Andhra is Swayambhu'?
nindian-history-113-16.x: The line on the Andhra Library Movement is Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah's.

nc04c434da36.s: The Quit India resolution adopted by the Congress Working Committee at Wardha on 14 July 1942 was proposed by:
nc04c434da36.x: The Wardha resolution was proposed by Nehru and seconded by Patel; the AICC ratified it at Bombay on 8 August 1942.

nindian-history-112-4.s: Who said, 'Partition fell on us like a bomb'?
nindian-history-112-4.x: Surendranath Banerjee said the partition fell like a bomb; 'Swaraj is my birthright' was Tilak's and 'Do or Die' Gandhi's.

nindian-history-97-24.s: Who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank during the Quit India Movement?
nindian-history-97-24.x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Kanaklata Barua was shot at Gohpur and Matangini Hazra fell at Tamluk.

n0e56fbdefc0.s: In 1942, when Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call, his paper was:
n0e56fbdefc0.x: Gandhi's paper in 1942 was Harijan; Young India had ceased publication in 1932.

nb393b1c5b87.s: Rangoon, whose fall formed part of the wartime background to Quit India, fell to Japan in:
nb393b1c5b87.x: Rangoon fell in March 1942 as the Japanese advance brought the war close to India's eastern frontier.

nindian-history-112-14.s: The slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' is associated with:
nindian-history-112-14.x: 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' is Shastri's slogan; 'Do or Die' is Gandhi's.

ne158baee2fc.s: How did the Communist Party of India fare in the 1945–46 elections after opposing the Quit India Movement?
o: It did not contest owing to a ban
It formed the government in Andhra
ne158baee2fc.x: The CPI lost heavily in 1945–46, against the background of its opposition to Quit India and support for the British war effort.

n6737a466941.s: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
n6737a466941.x: Chittu Pandey led the Ballia parallel government, which lasted about a week; Nana Patil and Y.B. Chavan were associated with Satara.

nedbef80e794.s: The coinage of the slogan 'Quit India' is generally credited to:
nedbef80e794.x: Yusuf Meherally is generally credited with coining 'Quit India'; Gandhi suggested the phrase in Harijan in April 1942.

n0683b85d002.s: The Jatiya Sarkar parallel government (December 1942 – September 1944) was set up at:
n0683b85d002.x: Jatiya Sarkar was at Tamluk; the Satara Prati Sarkar, linked to Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil, was the longest-lasting.

n46de21055ce.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra leaders during the Quit India Movement?
o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya, a CWC member, was jailed along with the CWC.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed for the first time in 1942.
Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground throughout.
The secret paper 'Quit India' spread the pamphlet 'Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi'.
n46de21055ce.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed again in 1942, not for the first time.

n12a62062d16.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Individual Satyagraha is correctly matched?
n12a62062d16.x: Vinoba Bhave was the first and Jawaharlal Nehru the second individual satyagrahi; the Congress ministries had resigned in November 1939.

nef4ab744589.s: The Quit India protest of Andhra University students demanding Gandhi's release was associated with:
nef4ab744589.x: The Andhra University protest was associated with Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya; Kakinada lawyers passed a similar resolution.

nd16599c43f1.s: The Andhra Circular, dated 29 July 1942, was seized by the police at:
nd16599c43f1.x: The Andhra Circular, prepared before the Bombay AICC meeting, was seized by the police at Kurnool.

n5cf30684cc5.s: During the Quit India Movement, the Congress Working Committee members were detained at:
n5cf30684cc5.x: CWC members were held at Ahmednagar Fort, while Gandhi was detained at the Aga Khan Palace, Pune.

n8c497c5faaa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under the Azad Hind Government?
o: The islands were handed over to the Azad Hind Government by Germany.
The Andaman Islands were renamed Shaheed Dweep.
The Nicobar Islands were renamed Swaraj Dweep.
Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943.
n8c497c5faaa.x: The islands were handed over by Japan, not Germany.

n2c19e445190.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)?
o: It declared war on Britain and the USA.
It was recognised by Japan, Germany and Italy.
It was proclaimed at Rangoon on 21 October 1943.
Its proclamation guaranteed religious liberty and equal rights.
n2c19e445190.x: The government was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943; Rangoon was where the INA headquarters later moved.

n5eb8c0e9e45.s: The August Offer of 1940 accepted ____ as the goal for India.
n5eb8c0e9e45.x: The August Offer accepted dominion status as the goal, proposed an expanded Executive Council and a war advisory council, and was rejected by the Congress.

n6f1df57b760.s: After the Tripuri session, the Pant Resolution required Subhas Chandra Bose to form the Working Committee according to the wishes of:
n6f1df57b760.x: The Pant Resolution required Bose to form the Working Committee in accordance with Gandhi's wishes.

n271c103bfdc.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah, a Forward Bloc member jailed for the article 'Chicharapidugu', was called Andhra Netaji.

n81ff32ee318.s: Subhas Chandra Bose resigned from the Indian Civil Service to join the Congress in:
n81ff32ee318.x: Bose qualified for the ICS in 1920 and resigned in 1921 to join the Congress.

n8001154505e.s: Who led the defence at the Red Fort INA trials (1945)?
n8001154505e.x: Bhulabhai Desai led the defence; Sapru, Nehru, Asaf Ali and K.N. Katju assisted.

n4253fabed72.s: Which greeting did Subhas Chandra Bose popularise in place of 'Bande Mataram'?
n4253fabed72.x: Bose popularised 'Jai Hind'; 'Dilli Chalo' was the INA war cry.

n83271053487.s: Matangini Hazra, shot while leading a flag procession during the Quit India Movement, was associated with:
n83271053487.x: Matangini Hazra was associated with Tamluk in Bengal; Kanaklata Barua was from Assam.

nbbdba5100ed.s: Which of the following was associated with the underground leadership of the Quit India Movement?
nbbdba5100ed.x: Lohia, with Jayaprakash Narayan, Sucheta Kripalani and Biju Patnaik, was part of the underground network; Desai and Sapru were linked to the INA trial defence.

n7f794144a8c.s: Subhas Chandra Bose escaped from house arrest in Calcutta in:
n7f794144a8c.x: Bose escaped from Calcutta in January 1941, travelled via Kabul and Moscow to Berlin, and reached Singapore in July 1943.

ne25d2904650.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RIN revolt of 1946?
o: Patel and Jinnah backed the continuation of the revolt.
Congress and Muslim League flags were hoisted together.
Bombay mill workers, railway workers and students joined the ratings.
Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists backed the ratings.
ne25d2904650.x: Patel and Jinnah persuaded the ratings to surrender; they did not back the revolt's continuation.

n2360b999754.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Royal Indian Navy revolt (1946) is INCORRECTLY matched?
n2360b999754.x: The revolt also spread to Karachi, so it was not confined to Bombay; it involved about 20,000 personnel, 78 ships and 20 shore establishments.

n48b48570a27.s: The sentence of transportation for life in the first INA trial was remitted in January 1946 by:
n48b48570a27.x: Commander-in-Chief Auchinleck remitted the sentences of Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Dhillon, who had been found guilty of waging war.

ncb7c491a3e1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Congress presidencies?
o: Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura session in 1938.
Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Tripuri session in 1939.
Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Lahore session of 1929.
Rajendra Prasad became Congress President in 1939 after Bose.
ncb7c491a3e1.x: The Lahore session of 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, not Gandhi.

n5fb23c41922.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: the facts carry no dates to order)
n5fb23c41922.s: Who founded the Servants of the People Society?
n5fb23c41922.x: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society; Mashriqi founded the Khaksars and Nehru the Independence for India League.

ned9403e36b2.s: Who became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953?
ned9403e36b2.x: Tanguturi Prakasam, who joined the Simon boycott in Madras and led the salt satyagraha at Devarampadu, became Andhra State's first Chief Minister in 1953.

nbb4112364cd.s: The Rampa movement is associated with:
nbb4112364cd.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa movement; Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan and Komaram Bheem the Gond movement.

nde382ac4075.s: Who presided over the Belgaum session of the Congress in 1924?
nde382ac4075.x: Gandhi presided at Belgaum (1924), Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur (1925), Ansari at Madras (1927) and Nehru at Lahore (1929).

n55fbb4ee473.s: Who paid the tribute to Gandhi: 'Generations to come... will scarce believe that such a one... walked upon this earth'?
n55fbb4ee473.x: The tribute is Albert Einstein's; Nehru said, 'The light has gone out of our lives.'

nindian-history-114-13.s: The Nationalist Party of 1934 is associated with:
nindian-history-114-13.x: Malaviya is linked with the 1934 Nationalist Party; the Swaraj Party with C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, and the Khaksars with Mashriqi.

nindian-history-118-10.s: The Drain Theory was propounded by:
nindian-history-118-10.x: Dadabhai Naoroji gave the Drain Theory; Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society.

nf4f956bff78.s: The Moderates who formed the National Liberal Federation left the Congress in:
nf4f956bff78.x: The Moderates left the Congress in 1918-19; Surendranath Banerjee was associated with the Federation's formation.

n694ff02c935.s: Mannathu Padmanabhan, known as Bharatha Kesari, founded the:
n694ff02c935.x: Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the Nair Service Society and took part in the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.

n46870910644.s: Gandhi gave C.F. Andrews the title:
n46870910644.x: Gandhi called C.F. Andrews 'Deen Bandhu'; Andrews lived with Gandhi at Phoenix and accompanied him to the Round Table Conference.

n13795d6b5b1.s: Gandhi compared the Cripps offer to a:
n13795d6b5b1.x: Gandhi called the Cripps offer a post-dated cheque.

n0408ca6edd9.s: Who was the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency?
n0408ca6edd9.x: Subramania Siva of Tamil Nadu, who took part in the 1908 Coral Mill strike with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, was the first political prisoner of the Presidency.

nindian-history-118-18.s: Which of the following belonged to the Extremist rather than the Moderate tradition?
nindian-history-118-18.x: Tilak was an Extremist leader; Naoroji, Gokhale and Sapru belonged to the Moderate or Liberal tradition.

nf54591bc057.s: Pingali Venkayya, whose flag design Gandhi endorsed at Vijayawada in 1921, was born at:
nf54591bc057.x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru. In the 1947 flag the Ashoka Chakra replaced the charkha.

nc037fa71a23.s: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a fast for Andhra State lasting:
nc037fa71a23.x: Potti Sriramulu died after a 58-day fast unto death for a separate Andhra State.

n89165e07120.s: Lala Lajpat Rai of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio presided over the Congress in:
n89165e07120.x: Lala Lajpat Rai, from Punjab, presided over the Congress in 1920.

nc549e63972b.s: Who founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin?
nc549e63972b.x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded the company; K. Kelappan was the 'Kerala Gandhi'.

n7dce6df560e.s: Who became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh?
n7dce6df560e.x: Sarojini Naidu, associated with Hyderabad and the Dharasana raid of 1930, became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.

nb3e975d69b7.s: Tej Bahadur Sapru is associated with the:
nb3e975d69b7.x: Sapru is associated with the Indian National Liberal Federation, which preferred constitutional cooperation to mass agitation.

naab8d96cb3f.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari' and Konda Venkatappayya 'Deshabhakta'.

ncc7fc742b77.s: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya' was a Gujarati rendering of:
o: Tolstoy's The Kingdom of God Is Within You
ncc7fc742b77.x: Sarvodaya was Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of Ruskin's Unto This Last.

n778bca605dc.s: Rani Gaidinliu of the Zeliangrong Heraka movement was given the title 'Rani' by:

n9a1ab9b64d9.s: Who was the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936)?
n9a1ab9b64d9.x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati of the Bihar Kisan Sabha was the first AIKS president; N.G. Ranga led the Andhra kisan movement.

nf985023d58d.s: Vallabhbhai Patel got the title 'Sardar' after the:
nf985023d58d.x: Patel was called 'Sardar' after the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, not Kheda.

n1d5c82217e8.x: Gandhi took the term 'Harijan' from Narsi Mehta, not Kabir.

n386fe644499.s: Who called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'?
n386fe644499.x: Subhas Chandra Bose called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'; Tagore called him 'Mahatma'.

n4dacd066afa.s: Who led the Vedaranyam salt march?
n4dacd066afa.x: C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam salt march; Bordoloi was the builder of modern Assam.

ne219d43d2d6.s: Who invited Gandhi on his 1920 Chhattisgarh tour?
ne219d43d2d6.x: Pandit Sundarlal Sharma invited Gandhi; Shaukat Ali accompanied him on the tour.

ndf7fbdb0a06.s: Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' in:
ndf7fbdb0a06.x: Nehru wrote The Discovery of India in Ahmednagar Fort jail; Gandhi's 'Songs from Prison' came from Yerwada.

n44b848e1eed.shape: one-liner (match not possible: the facts concern one person and do not form four pairs)
n44b848e1eed.s: Who headed the Congress Parliamentary Board that ran the 1937 provincial elections?
n44b848e1eed.x: As head of the Congress Parliamentary Board, Patel ran the 1937 elections and supervised the Congress ministries' discipline, elections and finances.

n3a9067edbce.s: The cut of the revenue increase to about 6 per cent after the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry was the outcome of the:
n3a9067edbce.x: The 6 per cent cut belongs to Bardoli (1928); Kheda ended with revenue suspended for poor peasants and confiscated property returned.

n8ee70ad69a8.s: Who was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India?
n8ee70ad69a8.x: Patel was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister and handled the States Department.

n7d460fefb77.s: Who referred the Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
n7d460fefb77.x: Nehru referred the issue to the UN, influenced by idealism and Mountbatten's advice, while Patel was sceptical and preferred a military solution.

na3665544a73.s: The Telangana armed struggle (1946-51) was withdrawn in:
na3665544a73.x: The struggle, led by the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha, was withdrawn in October 1951, not right after Operation Polo.

n179085fd6c8.s: Privy purses and royal titles were abolished by the:
n179085fd6c8.x: The 26th Amendment Act, 1971 abolished privy purses and titles, omitting Articles 291 and 362; the Rajpramukh office ended with the 7th Amendment.

nda63c9ebd29.s: Mir Osman Ali Khan, the ruler of Hyderabad at the time of integration, was which Nizam of the Asaf Jahi dynasty?
nda63c9ebd29.x: Mir Osman Ali Khan was the seventh Nizam of the Asaf Jahi dynasty, founded by Asaf Jah I in 1724.

n11b0272ace1.s: Operation Vijay (December 1961), which liberated Goa, was led by:
n11b0272ace1.x: Operation Vijay was led by Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth; J.N. Chaudhuri led Operation Polo in Hyderabad.

na1379796f96.s: The Razakars, the militant volunteer force of the Ittehad-ul-Muslimeen, were led by:
na1379796f96.x: The Razakars were led by Kasim (Qasim) Razvi; Laik Ali was the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad.

n15118474ac8.s: The Haripura Congress (1938) declared that Purna Swaraj covered:
n15118474ac8.x: Moving away from non-interference, the Haripura Congress (1938) declared that Purna Swaraj covered the states; Tripuri (1939) openly backed state movements.

n60ace5e9392.x: Laik Ali, the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad, wrote Hyderabad in Retrospect; V.P. Menon wrote The Story of the Integration of the Indian States.

n71f916d7c7b.s: The integration of Junagadh was resolved through:
o: An Instrument of Accession followed by war
n71f916d7c7b.x: Junagadh was resolved by a plebiscite, Hyderabad by police action, and Kashmir by an Instrument of Accession followed by war.

nc88f0e387d6.s: At the time of integration, Hyderabad was regarded as the ____ princely state.
nc88f0e387d6.x: Hyderabad was regarded as the largest and richest princely state and ranked first in population.

nee757316dc7.s: In the 1950 classification of states, Part D consisted of:
nee757316dc7.x: Part D was the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Part A were former Governor's provinces, Part B princely unions with Rajpramukhs and Part C Chief Commissioners' provinces.

naf546f09393.s: On 1 November 1956, the Marathwada region of Hyderabad State was transferred to:
naf546f09393.x: Marathwada went to Bombay State, the Telugu districts to Andhra Pradesh, and Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore.

nf299e53f654.s: Before Operation Polo, the Nizam of Hyderabad sought:
nf299e53f654.x: Mir Osman Ali Khan wanted Hyderabad to stay independent or accede to Pakistan.

n6e17e913cd7.s: Who was the Secretary and chief negotiator of the States Department headed by Sardar Patel?
n6e17e913cd7.x: V.P. Menon was Secretary and chief negotiator of the States Department, which Patel headed.

n663e6240975.s: How many policemen were killed when a crowd burnt the police station at Chauri Chaura in February 1922?
n663e6240975.x: At Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district (4 February 1922), the crowd burnt the police station and 22 policemen were killed; the NCM was then withdrawn by the Bardoli resolution.
